 Judgment

Though matter is listed for taking steps for respondent nos.1 and 2 for second time after recalling,
counsel for appellant was heard on merits of appeal.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 04.02.2017 passed by I Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'tribunal') in MVC No.729/2010, this appeal is filed.
3. It was submitted that main ground urged in appeal is that impugned order was passed mechanically.

It was submitted that an application was filed by appellant under Order XI Rule 14 of Code of Civil Procedure directing respondents to produce driving licence, permit and fitness certificate before tribunal.
Even when respondent/owner NC: 2023:KHC-K:8214 failed to produce same, tribunal has proceeded to pass award against insurer which called for interference.

4. From above, point that would arise for consideration is "Whether award calls for interference ?"
5.
Perusal of impugned award would indicate that application for direction to produce documents was not allowed.
Tribunal observed that prior to filing of said application, no notice calling upon respondents to furnish documents had been issued and therefore such application would in case be untenable.
On said reasoning, such contention was overruled.
It is also noted that insurer had not issued notice to insured calling for particulars about insurance policy, driving licence, permit and fitness certificate etc.
In absence of such effort, finding of tribunal based on police investigation records cannot be faulted.
Thus, there are no good grounds to interfere with impugned award.
Hence, point for consideration is answered in negative.
